lessons.title: The adapter family
objectives: Name the adapter, the SDK, or the connector
paragraphs: The technical requirements list Plus adapters for Agent Desktop Toolkit, Epic, Microsoft Dynamics 365, NetSuite, Oracle, Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Zendesk. They use HTTPS and Secure WebSocket. The desktop page says a pre-built adapter and Plus share the same underlying technology, and that a CRM SDK exists when you bring your own CRM.
The product API page also names Web Connectors. A connector that pops a URL is not the same object as a full Plus adapter. Say which one you deployed.

lessons.title: Salesforce versions move
objectives: Date every Salesforce version you copy
Do not keep IE for Salesforce
paragraphs: The technical requirements fetched for this lab say the Salesforce managed package is 2.46, SAML 2.0 is supported, and Lightning CTI is supported on Sales Cloud and Service Cloud for Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited, and Performance. Lightning Experience is supported for the Plus adapter.

2.46 is a line in a PDF, not a law. The next PDF can move it. Write 'as of the PDF we read' on any design that copies the number. Internet Explorer is ended except IE 11 for the Oracle Service Cloud adapter only, which is a different CRM.

lessons.title: SDK and connectors when there is no adapter
objectives: Use the SDK or a connector on purpose
paragraphs: The API product page lists a CRM SDK and web connectors beside the CTI, configuration, reporting, and statistics web services, plus Web2Campaign. The desktop page says bring your own CRM with the SDK.
A connector is a lighter pop. An SDK integration is code. Neither is maintained as a managed package by the Salesforce story. You own the tests when Five9 or the CRM moves.

lessons.title: Screen pop down, voice up
paragraphs: This is the signature adapter incident. The caller is heard. The record is not on screen. Causes you can cite: WSS blocked, TLS 1.1, the wrong CRM chapter, an unassigned campaign profile that was supposed to control pop-up behavior, or a connector pointed at a dead URL.
Campaign profiles can control pop-up windows. That is a second place, besides the adapter, where a pop is configured. Check both.

lessons.title: Salesforce modules inside the IVR
objectives: Say whether you mean the IVR module or the adapter
paragraphs: The IVR modules chapter includes a Salesforce module and an SFDC Einstein module, plus Contact Update and Lookup Contact Record. Those run in the script, before an agent exists. They are not the Plus adapter the agent uses after connect.

A design that 'integrates Salesforce' must say which of those it means. The ZIP example used a generic Query, not the Salesforce module. Use the Salesforce module when the target is Salesforce. Use Query when the target is some other service.
